# Messaging contract

The service owns two emitted subjects:

- `teacher.decision.recorded`, schema version `2`.
- `teacher.assistance.observed`, schema version `1`.

The approved target is a dedicated `TEACHER_EVENTS` JetStream stream, PostgreSQL transactional outbox, versioned event envelopes, and idempotent consumers. The existing `ms-go-course` best-effort publisher must not be copied.

The common envelope contains `event_id`, `event_type`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id`, `student_id`, `occurred_at`, `schema_version`, and `data`.

It consumes `course.plan.completed` and `course.plan.failed`, schema version
`1`, from `LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS` with durable
`ms-teacher-course-plan-outcome-v1` and queue
`ms-teacher-course-plan-outcome`. Only `source=TEACHER` outcomes have Teacher
side effects; Student/System planning is acknowledged without local state. A
Teacher outcome is accepted into `teacher_course_plan_notification_inbox`
before a bounded localized business notification is appended to the originating
Dialog, when `audit_refs.dialog_id` is present. The event ID is the Dialog
idempotency key, so a crash after Dialog commit is repaired by replay. Provider
errors, generated content, mastery, prompts, and chain-of-thought are excluded.

When `TEACHER_ONBOARDING_PATH_OUTCOME_ENABLED` is enabled and migration 022 is
installed, the service also consumes the exact
`planner.onboarding-path.outcome.v1` subject from `LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS`
with durable `ms-teacher-planner-onboarding-path-outcome-v1`. The strict v1
envelope uses `correlation_id=execution_id` and `causation_id=handoff_id`; the
data contains only the execution, exact S8 handoff, Student/Dialog/Teacher
identities, and `PATH_READY`, `ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS`, or `STATE_CHANGED`. The
first status requires course/path/first-lesson IDs and the conflict statuses
forbid them. Teacher resolves `handoff_id` through its immutable S8 ledger,
rejects identity drift, persists the event/execution inbox, and appends one
localized personal-teacher message using `event_id` as the Dialog idempotency
key. No Planner graph, profile, provider, raw error, or browser identifier is
accepted. Invalid contracts and identity drift terminate; transient database,
readiness, or Dialog failures retry.

It also consumes `learning_action.closed`, schema version `1`, from the `TASKANSWER_EVENTS` stream with durable `ms-teacher-learning-action-closed-v1`. This student-owned trigger contains `learning_action_id`, an action context, and zero to 100 frozen ordered targets. It deliberately contains no outcome, score, confidence, or mastery. Invalid/unknown/version-mismatched payloads are terminated; transient finalization failures are negatively acknowledged with delay.

The service consumes bounded `learning.activity.interesting`, schema version
`1`, from `LEARNING_ANALYTICS_EVENTS` with durable
`ms-teacher-learning-activity-v1`. The envelope correlates by analytics session
and contains only stable identities plus bounded counters. Student code,
compiler/test output, raw errors, mastery, and dialog history are excluded.
Invalid events terminate; transient persistence or Dialog failures are retried.
The inbox, explainable decision, and decision outbox commit atomically. When the
replaceable deterministic policy chooses an offer, it is appended to the same
general PersonalTeacher Dialog with the source event ID as idempotency key.
Only one offer may be delivered per student and analytics session; progress
signals stay silent.

The mounted consumer for `dialog.teacher.requested`, schema versions `1` and `2`, binds to
`DIALOG_EVENTS` with durable `ms-teacher-dialog-requested-v1` and queue
`ms-teacher-dialog-requested`. The Dialog-owned envelope contains only event,
source, dialog, student, PersonalTeacher, educational-context, and optional
LearningAction identities. Version 2 adds the positive dense
`teacher_turn_sequence`, canonical student message, correlation and Dialog
causation identities, with optional action-receipt and frozen reply metadata.
`student_command_id` is not part of version 2 and is rejected even when null;
Teacher derives or restores that private command identity after durable intake.
The envelope contains no body, mastery, or history; Teacher
loads a bounded window through the internal Dialog HTTP contract. Invalid JSON,
unknown fields, unsupported versions, and invalid context shapes terminate;
transient handler failures are negatively acknowledged with delay.

The subscriber acknowledges only after `teacher_dialog_job` durably inserts the
request or confirms that a redelivery is identical. Reuse of an event or source
message identity with different metadata is terminated as a conflict. General,
selected-text lesson, and action contexts are then processed asynchronously.

Generation and delivery are separately recoverable. The source event ID is the
stable confidential-execution and Dialog-append key. Decision, decision outbox,
and pending response body commit together; the body survives append retries and
is cleared after Dialog returns the verified committed message. Delivery remains
independent from asynchronous assistance evidence and mastery recalculation.

`teacher-turn-s0.v1` binds the source event, dense Teacher turn, Dialog,
canonical student message, source message sequence, student and PersonalTeacher,
correlation, and causation identities. Source message sequence is evidence only;
eligibility uses the dense per-Dialog Teacher sequence. The cursor advances only
after a confirmed delivered Teacher response or a durable `failed_no_effect`
proof and recoverable outcome. `unknown`, `partial`, and
`committed_unreconciled` remain blocking. AI Prompt is the only LLM boundary and
has no Student mutation authority.

The `data` payload for `teacher.decision.recorded` is the immutable `TeacherDecision` audit record. Version 2 adds `pedagogy_method`, `pedagogy_method_version`, and method-neutral `pedagogy_stage`, allowing methods to be replaced without losing audit identity. Task-scoped decisions include `learning_action_id` and use it as `correlation_id`. It contains context references and a bounded business reason, never chain-of-thought, prompts, raw student code, or dialog history.

The `data` payload for `teacher.assistance.observed` is one immutable assistance summary for one `learning_action_id`:

```json
{
  "learning_action_id": "action-cycle-uuid",
  "context_type": "lesson_task",
  "context_id": "task-id",
  "support_context": "guided",
  "hints_used": 2,
  "max_hint_level": 3,
  "intervention_used": false,
  "observations": [
    {
      "target": {
        "type": "concept",
        "key": "go.error-wrapping",
        "version": "optional-curriculum-version"
      },
      "kind": "hint_used"
    }
  ],
  "policy_version": "teacher-assistance-v1"
}
```

Allowed observation kinds are `independent_context`, `guided_context`, `hint_used`, and `intervention`. The target key is opaque and provider-neutral; `version` is optional until a canonical curriculum version is available. Success, failure, score, confidence, and mastery are forbidden teacher claims. `ms-go-student` combines these facts with its own objective outcomes later.

Policy `teacher-assistance-v1` emits one independent/guided context observation per target, plus hint and intervention observations when those actions occurred. With at most 100 targets, the event therefore contains at most 300 observations. A closure with no targets is committed to the teacher inbox only and produces no assistance event.

Delivery rules:

- decision and outbox envelope commit in one PostgreSQL transaction;
- relay delivery is at least once;
- `event_id` is sent as `Nats-Msg-Id`;
- relay claims use a lease long enough to cover the configured sequential batch timeout;
- each publication waits for a JetStream acknowledgement;
- retries use exponential delay from 1 second to 5 minutes and continue until acknowledged;
- there is no destructive dead-letter move in this increment; `last_error` and `attempts` remain queryable in the outbox;
- consumers must deduplicate by `event_id`;
- consumed closure inbox, optional assistance row, and optional emitted envelope commit atomically;
- consumed Dialog request is acknowledged only after durable job ownership or identical-duplicate verification;
- generated decision, decision outbox envelope, and pending Dialog response commit atomically;
- Dialog delivery retries use the source event ID and do not regenerate a staged response;
- interesting-activity inbox, intervention decision, and decision outbox commit atomically;
- proactive Dialog append uses the analytics event ID and is capped at one delivered offer per student/session;
- Learning Planner outcome acceptance is durable before Dialog delivery, and
  the plan event ID is the append idempotency key;
- `learning_action.closed.correlation_id` equals `learning_action_id`, and `teacher.assistance.observed.causation_id` equals the closure `event_id`.

Before adding another concrete producer or consumer, define:

- event owner and semantic version;
- stable event and causation identifiers;
- idempotent consumer behavior;
- payload and subject for each event;
- retry and dead-letter behavior;
- payload privacy and retention rules.

`ms-go-student` applies `teacher.assistance.observed` asynchronously through a durable inbox transaction. A response to the student does not wait for evidence projection or future mastery recalculation.
